title: Fixed-Preposition Verbs
definition: Some German verbs are commonly used with a specific preposition, and the preposition determines the case of the following noun or pronoun. Learn the verb and preposition together as one vocabulary unit.

rules.title: warten auf + accusative
rules.explanation: Use warten auf when waiting for a person or thing; auf takes the accusative in this fixed expression.

examples.english: I am waiting for the bus.

rules.title: denken an + accusative
rules.explanation: Use denken an to say that you are thinking about someone or something.

examples.english: I am thinking about my family.

rules.title: sprechen mit + dative
rules.explanation: Use sprechen mit when talking with a person.

examples.english: I am speaking with my teacher.
She is talking with her friend.

rules.title: sprechen über + accusative
rules.explanation: Use sprechen über when talking about a topic.

examples.english: We are talking about the film.
They are talking about their work.

rules.title: sich interessieren für + accusative
rules.explanation: Use sich interessieren für to say that someone is interested in something. The reflexive pronoun changes with the subject.

rules.title: Other useful verb-preposition pairs
rules.explanation: Memorize the preposition and case with each verb. Some verbs can take different prepositions with different meanings.

examples.note: Ich nehme an einem Kurs teil. — I take part in a course.
Kannst du mir bei den Hausaufgaben helfen? — Can you help me with the homework?
Ich bitte um Hilfe. — I ask for help.
Ich freue mich auf den Urlaub. — I am looking forward to the holiday.
Ich freue mich über das Geschenk. — I am happy about the gift.

verb_preposition_pairs.example: Ich nehme an einem Kurs teil.
Ich helfe dir bei der Arbeit.

common_mistakes.explanation: The fixed expression is warten auf + accusative.
Sich interessieren is reflexive and requires mich for ich.
Mit takes the dative; masculine dative mein becomes meinem.

mastery_goal: You can memorize common verb-preposition combinations and use the required case in simple sentences.
